title: TRAPPIST-1 — seven Earth-sized worlds, so close each hangs in its neighbor's sky

segments.en: Not a moon: the next planet. At its closest, it looks almost two and a half Moons wide.
segments.en_cap: Not a moon: | the next planet. | At its closest, | almost 2.5 Moons wide.

segments.en: TRAPPIST-1: seven Earth-sized worlds around one small red star, forty light-years away.

segments.en: Each beat is one planet crossing its star, sped up forty-three thousand times.
segments.en_cap: Each beat: | one planet | crossing its star, | sped up 43,000×.

segments.en: The star itself is barely bigger than Jupiter.
segments.en_cap: The star itself | is barely bigger | than Jupiter.

segments.en: Their years last from a day and a half to nineteen days.
segments.en_cap: Their years last | from 1.5 days | to 19 days.

segments.en: And all seven orbits would fit inside Mercury's, six times over.

segments.en: Planet E orbits where water could stay liquid. Its sun looks four times wider than ours.

segments.en: A year there lasts six days, and one side likely never sees night.
